devices.name: Banshee
devices.blurb: Wired Hatters dual-SoC (ESP32-C5 display + ESP32-S3). GhostESP firmware.

install.title: Flash both chips from the official flasher
install.detail: Open https://ghostesp.net/flasher in Chrome or Edge. Banshee needs Banshee_S3.zip on the compute chip and Banshee_C5.zip on the display chip. Do not use a Cardputer or generic GhostESP zip.

install.title: C5 self-OTA is off
install.detail: Since v2.1.2 the Banshee C5 updater partition was removed. Settings, Firmware Update on the C5 will not install a new image. USB flash is the path. The S3 can still take an update over GhostLink when that channel is offered.

install.title: Match the channel you meant to run
install.detail: Stable and prerelease are different tags. If you flash a pre zip, the version on the device should match that pre tag, not the stable one.

devices.recoveryTitle: Download mode if the wrong zip was flashed

recovery.title: BOOT and RESET on the chip you broke
recovery.detail: The S3 and the C5 enumerate separately. Hold BOOT on the chip that got the bad image, tap RESET (EN), and release BOOT. Use a data USB-C cable. The flasher should offer a serial port.

recovery.title: Reflash the matching Banshee zip
recovery.detail: Banshee_S3 only on the S3, Banshee_C5 only on the C5. If the screen is up but the radios are dead, you likely wrote the display image to the wrong chip, or the reverse. Download mode plus the correct zip is the undo.

backup.note: Banshee has two chips that show up as separate USB ports. Run the backup once for each chip. The file name records which chip it came from.

devices.name: Biscuit Pro
devices.blurb: Dual-chip ESP32-C5 + WROOM. Official Pro flasher reads the Biscuit_V1 manifest.

install.title: Use the phone app for a normal update
install.detail: Open Biscuit Manager, connect over BLE, and open the firmware notice on the Dashboard. Pick Production unless you mean to test Beta.

install.title: Give it Wi-Fi, then wait for both chips
install.detail: Enter the SSID and password the Biscuit itself should use. The C5 scanner updates first, then the WROOM gateway. Keep it powered and nearby until the app reconnects and both versions match.

install.title: USB reflash only if OTA will not start
install.detail: Install the CH340 or CP210x driver. Clone the flasher repo. Use a data USB-C cable and run python biscuit_pro_flash.py. It downloads the current cloud firmware and flashes both modules.

devices.recoveryTitle: Download mode if a flash fails

recovery.title: Put both modules in download mode
recovery.detail: Hold the boot buttons on the PCB, click reset, then release boot. If the ports do not show up, keep holding boot while you start the script. This is ESP download mode, not USB DFU.

recovery.title: Run the Pro flasher again
recovery.detail: python biscuit_pro_flash.py. It retries common failures. If nothing enumerates, swap the cable and port, reinstall the driver, and re-enter download mode before flashing a second time.

recovery.title: Do not mix Pro and Ultra scripts
recovery.detail: biscuit_pro_flash.py talks to the Biscuit_V1 manifest. The Ultra script is a different product path. Flashing the wrong package is how a dual-chip unit gets one side stuck.

backup.note: Dual-chip board. If two serial ports appear, back up each one.

devices.name: Biscuit Ultra
devices.blurb: Pro radios plus SD card and external antennas. Manifest: Biscuit_Ultra.

install.title: OTA from Biscuit Manager
install.detail: Same two-chip order as the Pro: C5 scanner, then WROOM gateway, over Wi-Fi credentials you type into the app. Production is the channel to leave on.

install.title: USB path uses the Ultra script
install.detail: Clone https://github.com/CodeHedge/biscuit_flasher and run python biscuit_ultra_flash.py. It pulls https://firmware.biscuitshop.us/Biscuit_Ultra/Prod/manifest.json and flashes both chips.

install.title: SD card is storage, not the flasher
install.detail: The Ultra SD slot holds PCAPs and evil-portal files. Firmware still comes from the app OTA or the Ultra USB script, not from dropping a bin on the card.

devices.recoveryTitle: Download mode if a flash fails

recovery.title: Boot buttons, then reset
recovery.detail: Hold the boot buttons, click reset, release boot so both the C5 and the WROOM enter download mode. Keep holding boot if the script cannot see a port.

recovery.title: Reflash with the Ultra script only
recovery.detail: python biscuit_ultra_flash.py after the CH340 or CP210x driver is installed. A charge-only cable looks like a dead device. Try another port before you erase anything else.

backup.note: Dual-chip board. If two serial ports appear, back up each one.

devices.name: Biscuit Crumb
devices.blurb: Smallest Biscuit: single ESP32-C5 wardriving and security-testing board. Manifest: Biscuit_Crumb.

install.title: Use the phone app for a normal update
install.detail: Open Biscuit Manager, connect over BLE, and open the firmware notice on the Dashboard. Pick Production unless you mean to test Beta.

install.title: Give it Wi-Fi, then wait
install.detail: Enter the SSID and password the Crumb itself should use. It has a single ESP32-C5, so there is only one update step. Keep it powered and nearby until the app reconnects and shows the new version.

install.title: USB reflash if OTA will not start
install.detail: Open the official Biscuit web flasher at flasher.biscuitshop.us in Chrome or Edge, choose Crumb, connect with a data USB-C cable, and flash. Run PenWare's backup first and close that tab so the flasher can use the USB port.

recovery.title: Reflash with the official web flasher
recovery.detail: Use flasher.biscuitshop.us and pick Crumb, not Pro, Ultra, DIY or Node. Each product has its own image.

recovery.title: Download mode if no port appears
recovery.detail: Try another data cable and USB port first. If the board still does not show a serial port, put the ESP32-C5 in download mode (hold BOOT while connecting USB) and start the flasher again. Ask in the official Biscuit Discord if the Crumb's buttons differ.

devices.name: Flipper Zero
devices.blurb: Official firmware, Momentum, Unleashed, and RogueMaster. Xtreme continues as Momentum.

companion.title: qFlipper screen stream (official remote)
companion.detail: Flipper does not ship an official emulator. qFlipper can stream the real screen and click the buttons: open Device information and click the Flipper picture. Repair and Install from file live in the same app.

install.title: Official: qFlipper Update
install.detail: Insert a microSD card. Install qFlipper from update.flipperzero.one. Connect USB and press Update. The Flipper reboots and finishes the install itself. Do not unplug until the desktop is back.

install.title: Momentum, Unleashed, or RogueMaster
install.detail: Download that project's update package from its GitHub release (.tgz). In qFlipper choose Install from file. The package lands on the SD card under /ext/update/ and the Flipper applies it on reboot. This path does not wipe the SD card.

install.title: One custom firmware at a time
install.detail: Momentum is the maintained continuation of Xtreme. Do not stack update folders from two customs. Install the one you mean to run, then read its version on the desktop.

devices.recoveryTitle: DFU recovery if an update breaks boot

recovery.title: From a working menu
recovery.detail: Main Menu, Settings, Power, Reboot, Firmware Upgrade, then press Right. qFlipper should see a DFU device.

recovery.title: If the screen will not boot
recovery.detail: Unplug USB. Hold Left and Back together, plug USB in while holding them, and release when qFlipper lists a DFU device. The screen may say DFU or stay dark.

recovery.title: Repair, then put your firmware back
recovery.detail: In qFlipper press Repair, or Install from file with flipper-z-f7-full-*.dfu from the official update server. SD card files stay. Repair installs official firmware. Reinstall Momentum, Unleashed, or RogueMaster afterwards if that is what you run.

items: In qFlipper, open Advanced and use Backup. It saves the Flipper's internal storage (settings, saved remotes, NFC/RFID/Sub-GHz captures) to your computer.
Copy the whole microSD card to your computer as well. Custom firmware updates keep the card, but a Repair does not protect files you care about.
Note which firmware you run (Official, Momentum, Unleashed or RogueMaster) so you can put it back after a Repair.

devices.name: FREE-WILi 2
devices.blurb: RP2350B multitool. Stock firmware is the bootloader. Releases are UF2/zip images.

install.title: Apps are not a full firmware flash
install.detail: The stock image is the bootloader. A UF2 dropped in the SD apps folder and launched from the menu does not replace FREE-WILi firmware. Use that path for apps and scripts.

install.title: Full image from the firmware repo
install.detail: Download FREE-WILi2-vXX.zip and its .sha256 from the GitHub release. Check the hash before you write it. Preview tags are pre-releases. Leave them off unless you mean to run one.

install.title: Read Help before a full rewrite
install.detail: docs.freewili.com covers the current button sequence and the onboard debug probe. Do not reuse a Flipper DFU or ESP32 BOOT hold on this board.

devices.recoveryTitle: Recovery if a firmware write fails

recovery.title: Use the FREE-WILi recovery page
recovery.detail: Open Help at docs.freewili.com and follow the recovery-mode steps printed there for this hardware revision. The onboard debug probe can also reprogram the RP2350B.

recovery.title: A bad app does not need a chip erase
recovery.detail: If a UF2 app fails, leave the menu and delete that file from the SD apps folder. The default firmware is what boots the menu. Only reflash the firmware zip when the menu itself will not start.

recovery.title: Do not flash the BSP hello apps over the stock image by accident
recovery.detail: The wilibsp fw flash tool is documented to refuse an image that would replace stock display firmware unless you force a development flash. Read that warning before you point it at the device.

items: Copy the SD card (apps and scripts folders) to your computer.
Keep the FREE-WILi2 zip and its .sha256 for the version you run now, so you can return to it.

devices.name: HackRF Pro H4M
devices.blurb: HackRF Pro with PortaPack H4M Pro. Mayhem firmware. Use the hpro package.

install.title: Download the hpro package
install.detail: From portapack-mayhem/mayhem-firmware releases, take the HackRF Pro files: COPY_TO_SDCARD_hpro_mayhem_*.zip for the card, or OCI_hpro_mayhem_*.ppfw.tar for the flasher. A plain HackRF One zip is the wrong board.

install.title: SD card update when Mayhem already boots
install.detail: Back up the card. Copy the hpro SD package onto a FAT32 card, insert it, and run the on-device firmware update. Nightlies use the same hpro names on the nightly-tag pre-release. Pro fixes often land there before the next stable.

install.title: No official emulator
install.detail: MayhemHub is a web companion for a HackRF you already have. It does not simulate the PortaPack. There is no official offline emulator.

devices.recoveryTitle: DFU full reset if a flash goes wrong

recovery.title: Pull the card and the coin cell
recovery.detail: Back up the SD card first. Remove the SD card and the coin cell and keep them from touching. The full reset erases settings.

recovery.title: HackRF Pro DFU looks dark
recovery.detail: Hold DFU and connect USB. On HackRF Pro the indicator lights all turn off. That is expected, and it is the opposite of some HackRF One DFU behavior. Other ways: hold RESET and DFU, release RESET first, then DFU. Or hold DFU, power on, release DFU, then plug USB.

recovery.title: Flash DFU, then Mayhem, without unplugging
recovery.detail: On Windows run mayhem_flasher.bat from the release package. Choose the HackRF Pro / PortaPack entry, then the option that writes DFU and Mayhem in one pass. On Linux or macOS use current hackrf host tools (distro packages are often too old). Do not disconnect between the two writes. Put the battery and the hpro SD contents back after it finishes.

items: Copy the whole SD card to your computer. Mayhem keeps settings, captures and apps there.
Keep the hpro package of the version you run now. PenWare's channel list links the release, so you can reflash the same version if a new one misbehaves.

devices.name: HaleHound
devices.blurb: HaleHound multi-protocol toolkit for Cheap Yellow Display (2.8"/3.5") and ESP32-DIV boards. Pick your exact board in the flasher.

install.title: Use the official web flasher
install.detail: Open flash.halehound.com in Chrome or Edge. Unplug other USB devices, connect the board with a data cable, pick your exact board from the menu, click Connect & Flash and choose the port. Unplug and replug when it finishes.

install.title: Pick the exact board
install.detail: HaleHound builds differ for CYD 2.8", CYD 3.5" and ESP32-DIV boards. The wrong build can boot to a blank or garbled screen. The GitHub release notes describe what changed; the flasher serves the matching firmware.

install.title: Back up first
install.detail: Run PenWare's backup before flashing, then close that tab so the flasher can use the USB port. Most CYD boards use a CH340 USB-serial chip; install the driver if no port appears.

devices.recoveryTitle: Download mode if the board will not flash

recovery.title: BOOT and RESET
recovery.detail: Hold BOOT, tap RESET (or plug in USB while holding BOOT), then release BOOT. The screen stays dark in download mode. Then start the flasher again.

recovery.title: Wrong screen or colors after flashing
recovery.detail: Reflash and pick the other board variant. First boot may ask for touchscreen calibration; inverted colors usually mean the wrong display build.

backup.note: CYD boards usually use a CH340 USB-serial chip. If more than one port appears, pick the one that appears when you plug the board in.

devices.name: Marauder V8
devices.blurb: ESP32 Marauder v8 (ESP32-C5). Stable release plus nightly. Binary suffix _v8.bin.

install.title: Confirm the PCB says v8
install.detail: v8 uses the 8 MB default_8MB layout and application offset 0x10000. A v6, v7, or Flipper bin will not boot it. The file you want ends in _v8.bin.

install.title: Prefer the JCMK Marauder Installer
install.detail: Open the JCMK Marauder Installer (link below) in Chrome or Edge. It selects bootloader, partition table, chip family, and offsets. Release notes have required the installer for v8 instead of an app-only bin. Run PenWare's backup first, then close that tab so the installer can use the USB port.

install.title: SD update only on a matching layout
install.detail: If the device already runs a compatible partition map, copy the _v8.bin to the top level of the SD card, rename it update.bin, and use the on-device firmware update menu. Back up the card first. Do not replace a working partition table unless you are doing a full install.

install.title: Nightly is a separate file from the same repo
install.detail: Nightlies are automated pre-releases. Grab the _v8.bin attached to that pre-release, not the stable asset. Treat them as test builds.

devices.recoveryTitle: Download mode if the wrong bin was flashed

recovery.title: Enter the ROM download boot
recovery.detail: Unplug USB. Hold BOOT, plug the data cable back in, then release BOOT. If the board has RESET, hold BOOT, tap RESET, and release BOOT. The screen stays blank. This is not HackRF DFU.

recovery.title: Full install, not the app bin alone
recovery.detail: A blank or boot-looping v8 needs bootloader, partition table, and the v8 application from the installer. An application-only .bin will not recover a wiped layout.

recovery.title: Leave it connected until the tool finishes
recovery.detail: Do not swap cables or tap reset mid-write. If the port disappears, re-enter download mode and start the installer again rather than power-cycling a half-written flash.

devices.name: Phantom
devices.blurb: Rabbit Labs Phantom. Marauder build for CYD 2432S024 Guition. File ends in _cyd_2432S024_guition.bin.

install.title: Confirm it is the Guition 2432S024
install.detail: Marauder calls this board RL Phantom. The asset ends in _cyd_2432S024_guition.bin. A 2432S028 CYD bin is a different panel and will not draw a UI.

install.title: Installer, then that exact file
install.detail: Use the JCMK Marauder Installer (link below) and select the Phantom / CYD Guition target. Nightly builds ship the same suffix on the pre-release. Do not flash the Marauder v8 bin onto this board.

install.title: USB port that enumerates serial
install.detail: CYD boards often have two USB-C ports. Use the one that shows a serial port, not a charge-only socket. A data cable is required.

devices.recoveryTitle: Download mode if the screen stays black

recovery.title: BOOT and RESET
recovery.detail: Hold BOOT, tap RESET, release BOOT. Or hold BOOT while plugging USB. The panel stays dark in download mode. That is normal.

recovery.title: Write the Guition bin, not another CYD
recovery.detail: If you flashed _cyd_2432S028 or a 2-USB build, go back to download mode and flash _cyd_2432S024_guition.bin from the same Marauder release. A full install includes bootloader and partitions, not only the app bin, when the unit no longer boots.

backup.note: Use the USB-C port that shows a serial port, not a charge-only one.

devices.name: T-Embed
devices.blurb: LilyGO T-Embed and T-Embed CC1101 running Bruce. Pick the matching target.

install.title: Identify CC1101 vs standard
install.detail: Look at the back of the board. A CC1101 radio means the T-Embed CC1101 build. No CC1101 means the standard T-Embed build. The other binary can boot to a blank screen.

install.title: Bruce web flasher
install.detail: Chrome or Edge: https://bruce.computer/flasher.html. Choose LilyGo, then T-Embed or T-Embed CC1101. Use the latest stable release unless you turned the prerelease watch on.

install.title: Download mode before Connect
install.detail: If the flasher asks: pull the battery if the board stays powered, hold the encoder center button, and press RST. On the CC1101, RST is on the board beside the ESP32-S3. Hold the encoder button until the port connects.

install.title: Blank screen after a good flash
install.detail: Disconnect USB. Do not use the side power button first. Open the back and tap RST once. If it is still blank, you picked the wrong T-Embed target. Re-enter download mode and flash the other one.

devices.recoveryTitle: Download mode if the wrong Bruce target was flashed

recovery.title: Encoder plus RST
recovery.detail: Remove the battery so the board cannot stay on. Hold the encoder center button, press RST, and keep holding the encoder until the browser flasher sees the port.

recovery.title: Erase and write the correct target
recovery.detail: In the flasher, check erase for a clean install, then flash LilyGo T-Embed or T-Embed CC1101. The version tag should match the Bruce release PenWare is showing. Stock LilyGO UI firmware is a different project.

devices.name: WiFi Pineapple Pager
devices.blurb: Hak5 Pager. Firmware is only official from the Hak5 download portal, not GitHub.

companion.title: Virtual Pager (official live UI)
companion.detail: There is no offline emulator. On the USB or management network, open http://172.16.52.1:1471 for a live screen, buttons, and a shell. Do not run a firmware upgrade from that shell. The upgrader stops the service that hosts it.

install.title: Download only from Hak5
install.detail: https://downloads.hak5.org/pineapple/pager is the only firmware source. Check the SHA-256 PenWare shows against the portal. Other people's bins can leave the Pager unable to boot.

install.title: Update on the device, or over SSH
install.detail: With client Wi-Fi, use the on-device software update and let it reboot. The first boot after an upgrade is slower. Without client Wi-Fi: scp the signed bin to /tmp, SSH in, and run INSTALL_FIRMWARE /tmp/<file>.bin.

install.title: GitHub is payloads, not firmware
install.detail: hak5/wifipineapplepager links the payload, theme, and ringtone repos. Do not flash those as firmware.

devices.recoveryTitle: Button recovery if it will not boot

recovery.title: Hold A, then power on
recovery.detail: Power the Pager off. Hold the green A button. Press the top power button for about 3 seconds and keep holding A. The green A LED blinks slowly. Connect a data USB-C cable to a computer.

recovery.title: Upload at the recovery page
recovery.detail: Open http://172.16.52.1 in a browser. Type http:// so the browser does not upgrade to https. Upload the Pager firmware you downloaded and install. This takes about 15 minutes and cannot be done over Wi-Fi.

recovery.title: Pager firmware only
recovery.detail: A Pineapple Nano, Tetra, or other Hak5 image will not run here and can make the unit unbootable. If you already flashed the wrong file, repeat this recovery with a Pager image from the portal.

items: Copy your loot and any custom payloads off the Pager (SCP over the USB network) before updating.
Firmware itself always comes from the Hak5 portal. Check the SHA-256 PenWare shows against the portal before installing.
